title: feat(pm): the queue guard refuses a project-thread Tier S record reviewed from the PR's own account
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DCP4SZZMWf3q3mM4d5VgXFh)_

Fixes #25415

## What changes

- `scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs`: two new readers. `readReviewedByAccount` reads a `Reviewed-by-account:` key line (in the file's one key-line convention), and it accepts exactly one GitHub login. A leading `@` is allowed; a bot login, prose, or two logins read `unreadable`. `readAttributionLogin` reads the `claude-projects-attribution` `github_login` from **any** line of a PR body. A marker with no readable login reads `unreadable`, never `absent`. `locateReviewOfRecord` now also returns `account`, read off the same comment it chose.
- `scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs`: the Tier S record leg reads the attribution from the PR body it already fetches (no new API call). A new pure function, `accountIndependence`, does the comparison. When the body carries the attribution line, a record that otherwise stands becomes `not-independent` (refused, exit 3) if the reviewer account equals the attribution login (case-insensitive), or if the account line is missing or unreadable, or if the attribution itself is unreadable. The refusal names both logins and the rule. The clear prints both logins it compared. A body **without** the line (Routine seats, humans) is `not-owed`, so today's reading is unchanged. The approval limb is untouched, so the leg stays monotone.
- Self-tests: there is a new guard battery (10 cases; floor 27 → 28) and a new recogniser battery (7 cases; floor 12 → 13). Guard: 344 cases pass. Recognisers: 208 cases pass. A mutation that turns the check off reds all 10 guard cases.

## Key name

This PR uses `Reviewed-by-account:`, as the card says. The paired skills card #25414 (draft PR #25422) writes the rule in prose ("记录独立性段并书两账户") and settles no key of its own. If it settles a different key, only `keyLineRegex('Reviewed-by-account')` and the refusal text change.

## Deviations from the card (premise drift)

- **`--pair` no longer exists.** Ruling record 5770886272 (#19061, letter B) retired the `--pair` landing pre-check. Its job of printing the two logins is now done by the guard's own clear and refusal lines.
- **The guard has no `--explain` flag.** In its place, here is an offline replay of #25363 at head `a6b929fa3`. The attribution reads `os-bill`. Record 6357150459 names the other account only in prose, so the reading is `account-missing` and the record **would be refused**. With `Reviewed-by-account: os-elon-musk` added, the reading is `holds`. (#25363 touched no governed path, so the guard never consulted its record in real life.)
- **`--template` does not print the new line yet.** Its output is pinned byte-for-byte across several batteries. The refusal text tells the seat exactly what to add.

## Gates

`dispatch-gates --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 35 families. All 35 ran with exit 0, and `--ran` reports `35 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED`. `check-governed-merges --test` on the two paths: NOT governed, so this is an ordinary queue landing. The workflow that runs the guard is unchanged.
